chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Sunnah has established that the jizyah (poll tax) is not taken from the insane person nor from the one whose intellect is overpowered.

key_terms.الْجِزْيَةُ: The poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects
key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبِ عَلَيْهِ عَقْلُهُ: The one whose intellect is overpowered/impaired

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from paying jizyah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that the exemption from jizyah for the insane (al-ma'tuh) and those with impaired intellect (al-maghlub 'alayhi 'aqluhu) is rooted in the principle of *taklif* (eligibility for religious obligation), as these groups lack the mental capacity to be held accountable. This ruling ensures that the poll tax is levied only upon those capable of managing their affairs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on justice and the removal of hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) in fiscal obligations.
